originalGroup.material:
Two lunch boxes

Lily and her brother Sam have two lunch boxes. Lily's box is yellow. Sam's box is green. Mum puts rice and eggs in the yellow box. She puts bread and cheese in the green one.

At school, Lily opens her bag. The green box is inside! Sam is in the classroom next door. Lily takes the box to him. Sam has the yellow one in his bag. They laugh and change boxes.

At lunch, Lily sits with her friend May. Sam sits with Ben. Each child now has the right lunch.

originalGroup.material:
The ball under the sofa

On a rainy afternoon, Max wants to play with his small football. He looks in the toy box, but it is not there. He looks behind the door. There is a shoe, but no ball.

His sister Amy is on the sofa with a book. "Look under here," she says. Max gets down on the floor. He sees the ball beside a red sock.

Max takes the ball to his bedroom. "No football in the living room, please," Dad says. Max puts it away. Then he sits beside Amy and reads with her.

originalGroup.material:
At the bird table

Nina visits her grandpa on Sunday. There is a little bird table in his garden. In the morning, they put some bird food on it. Then they go into the house and watch from the window.

Two small birds come to the table. A black cat walks into the garden. The birds fly up to a tree. Grandpa opens the back door, and the cat runs away.

After a few minutes, the birds come back. Nina draws them in her notebook. She does not go outside because she wants the birds to eat quietly.

originalGroup.material:
A chair for the garden

Dad paints an old chair blue. He puts it in the garden to dry. "Please do not sit on it yet," he tells Tom. Tom makes a sign. It says, "Wet paint!"

Tom puts the sign on the chair. Then he goes inside for a drink. When he comes back, the sign is on the grass. The wind is strong today.

Tom gets two clothes pegs from Mum. He uses them to hold the sign on the chair. Now the wind cannot take it away. Dad smiles. "Thank you for helping," he says.

originalGroup.material:
The library book

Ella goes to the school library after lunch. She wants a book about animals. The books about cats are on a low shelf. The books about birds are on a high shelf.

Ella can get a cat book, but she cannot reach the bird books. She asks Mr Green for help. He gives her a book with a blue bird on the front.

Ella borrows the bird book. She takes it home and reads it with Dad. On Friday, she brings it back. Next time, she wants to read about cats.

originalGroup.material:
A postcard for Aunt Rose

Finn draws a picture of his new house on a postcard. He wants to send it to Aunt Rose. Mum writes the address, and Finn puts a stamp in the corner.

They walk to the shop. There is a red post box beside it. Finn is too short to reach the opening. Mum lifts him, and he puts the card inside.

At the shop, they buy milk and bananas. Finn chooses one banana for his snack. On the way home, he asks, "Will Aunt Rose like my picture?" Mum smiles. "I think she will."

On the bus, she sees water on her bag. The bottle is open. She closes it and takes out the wet towel. Her pencil case is wet too, but the book in the front pocket is dry.

At school, Grace puts the towel beside the window. She tells her teacher what happened. At home that afternoon, she checks the bottle before putting it in her bag again.

Pip and the piano

Maya practises the piano after school. Her puppy Pip usually sleeps beside the kitchen door. Today he comes into the music room and sits on the rug.

Maya plays a fast song. Pip gets up and walks to the window. Then Maya plays a slow song. Pip lies down again and closes his eyes.

When Maya stops, Pip opens his eyes and looks at her. Maya laughs. "Do you want another song?" she asks. Mum comes in with some water for Pip. "He may just want a drink," she says.

On Tuesday, Leo waits for Dad outside the school gate. He has a red bag and a long ruler. His friend Joy waits with him.

A white car stops across the road. Leo waves, but it is not Dad's car. Dad has a blue car. The woman in the white car is Joy's mum.

Joy says goodbye and goes to her mum. Leo stays by the gate with his teacher. Five minutes later, Dad arrives in the blue car. Leo puts his bag on the back seat and keeps the ruler in his hand.

Stars for the window

Ava and her cousin make paper stars at Grandma's house. Ava uses yellow paper. Her cousin uses blue paper. They make six stars: four yellow and two blue.

Grandma gives them some string. They put three stars on one string and three on another. Ava holds the first string near the window. It is too long, so Grandma cuts it a little.

The children hang both strings in the window. Then they put the small pieces of paper in a box. Grandma can use the pieces to make cards another day.

The children hang both strings in the window. Then they put the small pieces of paper in a box. Grandma can use the pieces to make cards another day.
